sentences.text: The type species of Undorosaurus grew to be 4 to 6 meters long.
Vladimir M. Efimov named the genus Undorosaurus in 1999, with Undorosaurus gorodischensis as the type species.
The genus was first known from holotype UPM EP-II-20 (527), a partial skeleton with a partial skull preserved in three dimensions.
The holotype was collected near the Volga River at Gorodischi from the Epivirgatites nikitini ammonoid zone of the Late Jurassic.
The species U. trautscholdi was discovered in 1878 by Hermann Trautschold and formally described in 2014 based on a partial left forefin from Mnyovniki, Moscow Oblast.
The third species, U. kielanae, was first described by Daniel Tyborowski in 2016 as Cryopterygius kielanae from the Kcynia Formation in Poland.
Undorosaurus belongs to the family Ophthalmosauridae.
Chris McGowan and Ryosuke Motani (2003) identified an incompletely fused ischiopubis and remarkably strong dentition as key differences from Ophthalmosaurus, supporting Undorosaurus as a valid genus.
Zverkov and Efimov (2019) treated the genus Cryopterygius as a junior synonym of Undorosaurus.
Undorosaurus lived from the Oxfordian to the Tithonian stages, between 161.5 and 143.1 million years ago.
It is debated whether Cryopterygius kristiansenae is synonymous with Undorosaurus gorodischensis.
